items.stem: A client at 28 weeks gestation arrives with sudden bright red vaginal bleeding and a soft, nontender uterus. Placenta previa has not yet been excluded. Which action is correct?

options.text: Defer digital cervical examination until ultrasonography rules out placenta previa, because digital exam may provoke massive bleeding.
Perform a vigorous digital cervical exam immediately to estimate dilatation before any imaging.
Discharge home without assessment because third-trimester bleeding is always normal.
Encourage unsupervised intercourse to promote placental migration.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: if bleeding occurs after 20 weeks, pelvic examination by digital cervical examination is contraindicated until previa is first ruled out by ultrasonography. OpenStax: vaginal exams should be avoided with known previa or vaginal bleeding to prevent additional injury.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Merck warns digital exam may cause sudden massive bleeding when previa is present.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Third-trimester bleeding requires urgent evaluation for previa versus abruption.
rationales.D: Incorrect. Sexual activity is restricted with previa; it does not safely 'migrate' the placenta.

items.stem: A client of reproductive age with a positive pregnancy test develops sudden severe unilateral pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, syncope, tachycardia, and hypotension. Ultrasound shows no intrauterine pregnancy. Complete the bowtie: priority condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.

conditions.text: Ruptured ectopic pregnancy with hemorrhagic (hypovolemic) shock
Stable, asymptomatic early intrauterine pregnancy without bleeding

actions.text: Establish large-bore IV access and begin ordered volume resuscitation while preparing for emergent surgical management
Notify the provider/surgical team immediately for unstable ruptured ectopic pregnancy
Discharge home with only oral antacids and no follow-up
Encourage unsupervised heavy exercise before evaluation
Give intramuscular methotrexate as first-line therapy while the client remains hemodynamically unstable

parameters.text: Blood pressure, heart rate, and signs of ongoing hypovolemia/shock
Abdominal/pelvic pain trend, bleeding, and neurologic status (alertness/syncope)

rationales.K1: Correct. Merck: ectopic pregnancy can rupture with hemorrhagic shock. OpenStax: bleeding, pelvic pain, syncope, or shock may signal rupture.
rationales.K2: Incorrect. Allergic rhinitis does not explain shock with positive pregnancy test.
rationales.K4: Incorrect. Findings indicate extrauterine pregnancy with instability, not a stable IUP.
rationales.A1: Correct. OpenStax hypovolemic shock care emphasizes volume resuscitation; Merck/OpenStax: unstable ectopic requires surgical management.
rationales.A2: Correct. OpenStax: unstable clients require emergent surgical intervention for rupture risk.
rationales.A3: Incorrect. Discharge without care is unsafe in suspected ruptured ectopic.
rationales.A5: Incorrect. OpenStax: methotrexate is for selected hemodynamically stable clients, not unstable rupture.
rationales.P1: Correct. Vital signs track hypovolemic shock response (OpenStax hypovolemic shock; Merck rupture hemorrhage).
rationales.P2: Correct. Pain, bleeding, and neurologic status reflect ongoing hemorrhage (both sources).

items.stem: A term newborn of a mother with insulin-treated diabetes is otherwise well. Which nursing action best helps prevent symptomatic neonatal hypoglycemia in the early hours after birth?

options.text: Support early, frequent enteral feedings (e.g., breast-feeding initiation soon after birth) and follow facility glucose-monitoring policy for at-risk newborns.
Withhold all feedings for 12 hours to 'rest' the pancreas.
Give only free water bottles and delay any calorie source.
Encourage prolonged cold exposure to increase metabolic demand.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: well at-risk neonates should receive early, frequent feedings; infants of diabetic mothers may develop transient hypoglycemia and are given oral or IV glucose. OpenStax: IDM are at risk; encourage early breast-feeding and timely feeding/glucose.
rationales.B: Incorrect. Delayed feeding increases hypoglycemia risk (Merck: delayed feeding is a common cause).
rationales.C: Incorrect. Free water without calories does not prevent hypoglycemia.
rationales.D: Incorrect. OpenStax links cold stress to depleted glucose stores; warmth and early feeding are preferred.

items.stem: An older adult reports infrequent, hard stools related to low activity and low fibre intake. Which teaching priority is most appropriate initially (assuming no red-flag surgical abdomen)?

options.text: Increase dietary fibre with adequate fluids and encourage regular physical activity as tolerated.
Stop all oral fluids to 'dry out' the bowel.
Eliminate all fruits and vegetables permanently.

items.stem: A client is starting clozapine for treatment-resistant schizophrenia. Which teaching and monitoring points are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) monitoring is required because clozapine can cause severe neutropenia.
Severe neutropenia increases the risk of serious infection.
Report fever or other signs of infection promptly to the provider.
Laboratory blood monitoring can be skipped indefinitely after the first dose.
Doubling the dose whenever a fever starts is the preferred self-management plan.
Clozapine has no hematologic risks, so infection precautions are unnecessary.

rationales.A: Correct. DailyMed boxed warning requires baseline ANC; OpenStax notes REMS monitoring of WBC/ANC for clozapine.
rationales.B: Correct. DailyMed: severe neutropenia is associated with increased risk of serious and fatal infections; OpenStax lists agranulocytosis/neutropenia among hematologic effects.
rationales.C: Correct. Infection risk with neutropenia requires prompt reporting of fever/infection signs (supports DailyMed infection risk + OpenStax hematologic monitoring).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Ongoing ANC monitoring is required; it is not a one-time check.
rationales.E: Incorrect. Dose escalation for fever is unsafe and not indicated.
rationales.F: Incorrect. Hematologic toxicity is a major boxed warning.

items.stem: A client with known Graves disease develops high fever, marked tachycardia, severe agitation/confusion, vomiting, and diarrhea after an acute infection. Which interpretation and priority nursing action are best?

options.text: Suspect thyroid storm — a life-threatening emergency — initiate cardiac/airway monitoring and support, and prepare for ordered antithyroid therapy plus supportive measures (e.g., cooling, fluids) while treating the precipitant.
Reassure that these findings are expected mild seasonal allergies requiring only outdoor jogging.
Stop all monitoring and discharge immediately without evaluation.
Apply only topical antifungal cream as definitive endocrine therapy.

rationales.A: Correct. Merck: thyroid storm is a life-threatening emergency with fever, marked restlessness/confusion, GI symptoms, and tachycardia; treatment includes PTU, beta-blockade, cooling, fluids, and treating the cause. OpenStax: thyroid storm is a medical emergency managed with antithyroid medications and supportive care.
rationales.B: Incorrect. This presentation is not mild allergy.
rationales.C: Incorrect. Delaying care risks fatal arrhythmias/organ failure (OpenStax).
rationales.D: Incorrect. Antifungals do not treat thyrotoxic crisis.

items.stem: A 12-hour-old at-risk neonate has a confirmed low serum glucose and is becoming lethargic with poor feeding. Which intervention is the priority?

options.text: Begin prompt enteral feeding if the infant can feed safely, or administer ordered IV dextrose, and continue glucose monitoring.
Withhold all glucose sources for 8 hours to stimulate gluconeogenesis alone.

rationales.C: Incorrect. Ice chips provide no effective glucose replacement.
